# RQ6: order-flow imbalance and short-term price moves

*Generated by `python -m hftsim.research rq6` on 2026-11-16.*

> **Simulation evidence only.** These numbers describe the hft-sim synthetic market (docs/STYLIZED_FACTS.md §5 and docs/MARKET_MAKING.md §7 list its artefacts, notably RISKS K21 and K23). They are not evidence about any real market.

**Question.** How much of the short-term mid change does order-flow imbalance explain, and how does its impact scale with depth?

**Design.** The background with 0 or 30 informed traders, no market maker. Over consecutive intervals of 0.1, 1 or 10 s, the mid change (ticks) is regressed on the order-flow imbalance of the best quotes (Cont, Kukanov & Stoikov 2014), one regression per run. Each cell: seeds 2026–2033 (the same seeds in every cell), 180 simulated seconds, everything measured over the window 60–180 s. Values are means over seeds with 95% Student-t intervals in brackets; money in dollars.

| background | informed traders | interval | intervals per run | β (ticks per 1,000 shares) | R² | average top-of-book depth (shares) | β × depth |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

In CKS's stylised book (the same depth D at every level) ΔP = OFI / (2D), so β × depth ≈ 0.5; comparing the regimes checks whether β scales with 1/depth.

### Return autocorrelation in the same runs (no market maker)

| background | informed traders | lag-1 autocorrelation of 1 s returns | variance ratio (10 s / 10 × 1 s) |

| default | 0 | -0.205 [-0.253, -0.158] | 0.98 [0.80, 1.16] |
| default | 30 | -0.089 [-0.157, -0.021] | 0.97 [0.59, 1.35] |
| zero-intelligence | 0 | -0.048 [-0.124, 0.028] | 0.97 [0.76, 1.18] |
| zero-intelligence | 30 | -0.073 [-0.154, 0.008] | 0.85 [0.58, 1.11] |

**Reproducibility.** 32 runs of hftsim 0.1.0. `rq6.manifests.json` holds each run's complete flags and event digest; `hftsim run <flags>` reproduces the digest. Check: the first run (seed 2026) was re-run without the cache and reproduced digest `0xaf1d5fa3c1f7c83a`.
